comparisons.interpretation: Both state a healthcare-for-all goal. Bohren specifies single payer; Baria's broader answer does not establish the same financing mechanism or an opposing one.
Bohren names single-payer financing; Sherman names Medicaid expansion and changes in care delivery. The proposals differ, but Sherman does not explicitly reject single payer in this answer.

Bohren emphasizes a left platform and mobilizing overlooked voters; Baria emphasizes legislative experience, business knowledge and social justice. This is stated campaign framing, not a measure of actual effectiveness.

Bohren argues against a centrist strategy aimed at Republican crossover voters; Sherman foregrounds cross-aisle work and private-sector problem-solving. Their actual words establish the contrast without inferring it from their occupations alone.
